newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill would boost class-size reduction funds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill would boost class-size reduction funds.

text.p: A California state legislator introduced a bill on Wednesday that would increase state funding for class-size reduction by up to $800 million.
Under Assemblywoman Valerie Brown's proposal, the state would provide local school districts with $800 per pupil to help fund class-size reduction, compared with $650 per pupil in the current year.
Should the legislation be enacted, the changes would increase state spending by a maximum of $800 million in fiscal year 1997-98, Brown's office estimated.
